notes: Groceries taxed at 5% from July 1, 2025 (7% before).
Motor fuel is exempt from the general sales tax (per-gallon excise instead).
Mississippi has no general local sales tax; some cities levy tourism taxes on restaurants (not included).
Tobacco is assumed taxed at the general rate (excise taxes left out); not verified state by state.
gaps: Mississippi counties have no general sales tax; Jackson is the only city with a general one (1%).

"meals_local" holds local tourism taxes on restaurant sales (usually 1%-3%), read from the DOR's description of each levy; hotel-only levies are not recorded. Where a city has more than one restaurant levy their rates are added.
Groceries are taxed at 5% instead of 7% (state); that is a taxability question, not part of the general rate.
Restaurant levies on part of a city only are not recorded: Pearl (West) Restaurant Tax
Restaurant levies not matched to a place or county (not recorded): Columbus-Lowndes Community Development Tax
